content_paraphrased: Order positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions; use the symbols =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥
teaching: Integers and negative decimals on a number line; ordering mixed fractions, decimals and percentages by converting to decimals; < and ≤ used in error intervals
gap: ≠, >, ≥ not assessed as a standalone skill

content_paraphrased: Apply the four operations, including formal written methods, to integers, decimals and simple fractions (proper and improper) and mixed numbers, all both positive and negative
teaching: Negatives; fraction and mixed-number arithmetic; decimal add/subtract/multiply/divide; long multiplication; short and long division; dividing by a decimal
gap: Written-method layout is taught but not marked: only final answers are checked

content_paraphrased: Recognise and use relationships between operations, including inverse operations; use conventional notation for priority of operations, including brackets, powers, roots and reciprocals
teaching: Priority with brackets, powers and perfect-square roots; equal priority left to right; inverse operations; cancellation when multiplying fractions

content_paraphrased: Use the concepts and vocabulary of prime numbers, factors, multiples, common factors, common multiples, HCF, LCM and prime factorisation, including product notation and the unique factorisation theorem
teaching: Primes, factor pairs, factor trees, index form, unique factorisation, Venn diagram HCF/LCM, contexts

content_paraphrased: Use positive integer powers and associated real roots (square, cube and higher); recognise powers of 2, 3, 4, 5
higher_only_part: Higher: estimate powers and roots of any given positive number
teaching: Squares, cubes, powers of 2, 3 and 10, square and cube roots, combined calculations; Higher: locating roots between consecutive integers
gap: Higher roots beyond cube roots; estimating to a decimal place

content_paraphrased: Calculate with roots, and with integer indices
teaching: Multiply/divide/power-of-power laws, zero index, negative indices; Higher: fractional indices including negative fractional
gap: Algebraic indices follow in the Algebra strand

content_paraphrased: Calculate exactly with fractions and multiples of π
teaching: Exact fraction calculation with simplest-form answers

content_paraphrased: Calculate with and interpret standard form A × 10^n, where 1 ≤ A < 10 and n is an integer
teaching: Large and small numbers both ways; correcting non-standard form; comparing; multiply, divide, add and subtract with adjustment

content_paraphrased: Work interchangeably with terminating decimals and their corresponding fractions
higher_only_part: Higher: change recurring decimals into fractions and vice versa
teaching: Terminating decimal ↔ fraction ↔ percentage; Higher: recurring decimals to fractions (one, two and mixed recurring digits)
gap: Fraction → recurring decimal direction (Higher) not yet assessed

content_paraphrased: Identify and work with fractions in ratio problems
Interpret fractions and percentages as operators
teaching: Fractions of amounts, reverse fractions, fraction of a fraction; percentages of amounts including over 100% and decimal percentages; one amount as a percentage of another
gap: Percentage change and reverse percentages belong to R9 (Ratio)

content_paraphrased: Use standard units of mass, length, time, money and other measures, including standard compound measures
Estimate answers; check calculations using approximation and estimation, including answers obtained using technology
teaching: Rounding each number to 1 significant figure; division by numbers less than 1; deciding over- or underestimate
gap: Estimates are marked against the 1 s.f. method the questions instruct

content_paraphrased: Round numbers and measures to an appropriate degree of accuracy (decimal places, significant figures); use inequality notation to specify simple error intervals due to truncation or rounding
teaching: Rounding to 10/100/1000, decimal places and significant figures with required trailing zeros; error intervals for rounding and truncation

content_paraphrased: Apply and interpret limits of accuracy
teaching: Limits of accuracy as error intervals; Higher: bounds of sums, differences, products and the choice for quotients
gap: Bounds of quotients assessed by choice, not calculation
